tools.name: is-card-safe
tools.description: Check payment-card brand, length and Luhn checksum. Use with synthetic card numbers in payment-form tests. Returns {ok, normalized?, brand?, last4?, issues}; not a payment authorization or fraud check.

tools.name: is-email-safe
tools.description: Check conservative ASCII email address syntax. Use to reject malformed addresses in forms and test fixtures. Returns true or false; does not check mailbox existence or deliverability.

tools.name: is-iban-safe
tools.description: Check IBAN country rules, length and checksum against a bundled registry. Use to screen public or synthetic IBANs in test data. Returns {ok, normalized?, issues}; does not verify account ownership or transferability.

tools.name: is-iso-date-safe
tools.description: Check Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates, including leap days. Use for date-only form fields, not timestamps or timezone offsets. Returns true for a valid date, otherwise false.

tools.name: is-ip-safe
tools.description: Check IPv4 or IPv6 literal-address syntax. Use to screen candidate IP strings, not test reachability or geolocation. Returns {ok, version, issues}; version is 4, 6 or null.

tools.name: is-json-safe
tools.description: Parse JSON with bounded depth, key counts and input size. Use to screen JSON without execution; use optimize-dataset for JSONL or CSV cleanup. Returns {ok, issues, bytes, depth, keys, value?}; parsed value is included only when valid.

tools.name: is-password-safe
tools.description: Evaluate password strength using local heuristics. Use only with dummy passwords when testing password policies. Returns {ok, score, entropyBits, length, sets, reasons, suggestions}; no breach-database lookup.

tools.name: is-phone-e164
tools.description: Check phone number syntax against E.164 after local normalization. Use to test international number formats, including spaces or 00 prefixes. Returns true or false, not the normalized number; no subscriber or reachability check.

tools.name: is-uuid-safe
tools.description: Check canonical UUID syntax and optional RFC variant/version. Use to validate UUIDs; use generate-token to create them. Returns true or false; does not check uniqueness or resource existence.

tools.name: is-url-safe
tools.description: Check absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL syntax. Use to screen links before display or storage. Returns true or false; does not visit or assess the site's safety.

tools.name: is-us-tin-safe
tools.description: Check synthetic US EIN, SSN or ITIN number formats. Use with tax-ID input fixtures, never real personal identifiers. Returns {ok, normalized?, type, issues}; does not verify IRS issuance or identity.

tools.name: is-vat-safe
tools.description: Check country-specific VAT number patterns. Use to screen VAT fixtures before form submission. Returns {ok, country?, normalized?, issues}; no VIES lookup or active-registration check.

tools.name: optimize-dataset
tools.description: Clean and compact JSON, JSONL or CSV rows. Use for small datasets; use is-json-safe to check JSON syntax without changes. Returns text in the selected format; trims strings, deduplicates rows and may drop mostly empty columns.

tools.name: optimize-google-tag
tools.description: Rebuild GA4 gtag.js markup from a G- measurement ID. Use on existing GA4 snippets, not GTM containers or consent setup. Returns replacement HTML with async loading and a config call, or original input if no G- ID exists. Review lost settings and consent.

tools.name: minify-html
tools.description: Remove comments and compact whitespace in HTML fragments. Use for small, controlled HTML snippets, not full document compilation. Returns an HTML string; preserves pre, textarea, script and style contents. Regression-test rendered output.

tools.name: minify-js
tools.description: Compact small JavaScript snippets. Use for basic source cleanup, not AST-aware production minification. Returns JavaScript text, sometimes unchanged for complex syntax; regression-test its behavior.

tools.name: minify-css
tools.description: Reduce whitespace in CSS snippets. Use for basic stylesheet cleanup rather than production minification. Not a full CSS parser; visually test the result.

tools.name: minify-prompt
tools.description: Normalize prompt whitespace and line breaks. Use to compact formatting before calling a model; filler phrases are not removed. Returns trimmed text with normalized spacing; review prompts where whitespace carries meaning.

tools.name: strip-ansi
tools.description: Strip terminal ANSI escape codes from text. Use to make colorized logs readable for indexing or display. Returns plain text without interpreting log entries.

tools.name: generate-avatar
tools.description: Create an SVG placeholder profile icon. Use for synthetic avatars in demos and UI prototypes. Returns SVG markup, not a photorealistic likeness.

tools.name: generate-card-number
tools.description: Generate a synthetic payment-card fixture. Use for payment-form UI tests requiring a Luhn-valid card number. Returns {number, brand, expiry, cvc}; values are synthetic, not issued credentials.

tools.name: generate-color
tools.description: Generate a palette from a base color and harmony scheme. Use for design prototypes; defaults: random base, triadic scheme, five hex colors. Returns {base, scheme, colors, textOnBase}; text color is heuristic, not a WCAG contrast check.

tools.name: generate-dataset
tools.description: Generate synthetic rows as JSON, JSONL or CSV. Use for data import/export tests; use generate-fake-data for preset people or company fixtures. Returns at most eight records without accessing a database.

tools.name: generate-fake-data
tools.description: Create fictional users, companies, addresses or rows. Use to seed demos with preset records; use generate-dataset for custom fields. Synthetic values are not verified identities.

tools.name: generate-hash
tools.description: Compute SHA-256 or legacy MD5 text digests. Use for non-secret content fingerprints; generate-token creates new IDs instead. Returns a hex digest; unsuitable for password storage or key derivation.

tools.name: generate-lorem
tools.description: Generate lorem ipsum placeholder copy. Use for mock layouts needing filler words, sentences or paragraphs. Returns synthetic copy, not sourced editorial content.

tools.name: generate-password
tools.description: Generate random or seeded test passwords. Use for demo login fields; use generate-token for identifiers. Seeded values are predictable and visible to MCP clients; not a secure credential vault.

tools.name: generate-phone-number
tools.description: Generate fictional US-format phone numbers. Use for US demo phone fields; when supplied, city selects a local area-code pool and must match state. Returns an array of fictional (AAA) 555-01XX numbers; no subscriber lookup.

tools.name: generate-prompt
tools.description: Fill a prompt template with supplied variables. Use {name} placeholders with matching vars.name; missing variables become empty text. Returns a prompt string without invoking a model; code/image modes can add framing.

tools.name: generate-slug
tools.description: Convert a title into a Unicode-aware URL slug. Use when forming new path segments from headings. Inspect output before publishing permanent URLs.

tools.name: generate-ssn
tools.description: Generate fictional US SSN-style test identifiers. Use for SSN test fields; use generate-fake-data for mixed-record fixtures. Returns a string for count=1, otherwise an array; structural validity does not confirm issuance.

tools.name: generate-token
tools.description: Generate token strings or UUIDs. Use for test identifiers; use generate-password for password fixtures. Seeded output is predictable and unsuitable for authentication credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: is-card-safe, is-email-safe, is-iban-safe, is-ip-safe, is-url-safe, is-us-tin-safe, is-vat-safe · Private data: is-password-safe, is-uuid-safe, minify-html, generate-card-number, generate-dataset, generate-fake-data, generate-hash, generate-password, generate-ssn, generate-token · Public sink: is-email-safe · Destructive: optimize-dataset, minify-html, generate-phone-number.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: is-card-safe, is-email-safe, is-iban-safe, is-ip-safe, is-url-safe, is-us-tin-safe, is-vat-safe · Private data: is-password-safe, is-uuid-safe, minify-html, generate-card-number, generate-dataset, generate-fake-data, generate-hash, generate-password, generate-ssn, generate-token · Public sink: is-email-safe · Destructive: optimize-dataset, minify-html, generate-phone-number

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
